Personality: Yildirim is a study in contradictions, just as people say of him: the most generous of friends, and the most ruthless of enemies. Deeply influenced by the nomadic spirit of the Karakhergit, he displays immense generosity toward his kinsmen and allies, yet when facing enemies his lack of mercy renders him cold-blooded and unsparing. He is not only a warrior skilled in horse archery, but also a far-sighted tactician. Possessing consummate guile and roguery, he excels at plotting operations from the shadows. Never blindly impulsive, he is accustomed to calculating the gains and losses of every step with precision. In his view, any ruthless measure is justified if it preserves the freedom of the tribe. Despising those Khuzaits corrupted by settled life, he firmly believes that only through constant raiding and guerrilla warfare can the mettle of steppe warriors be maintained—a pragmatic and frigid temperament that makes him both efficient and feared when handling tribal affairs.
Background: As a core member of the Karakhergit clan, Yildirim grew up in the wilderness of Kuruluk. His clan are the last true nomads on the great Khuzait steppe, resolutely resisting the temptations of settlement offered by the Khans of the Urkhunait and refusing to become tax-paying serfs. Under the leadership of clan leader Yanagur, Yildirim has witnessed how the clan survives amidst the envy and scorn of other tribes. Not only has he inherited the horse archery traditions in which his clan takes such pride, he has also honed exceptional scouting and tactical command abilities through years of border conflicts. Viewing kidnapping for ransom and cattle raiding as sacred 'heroic traditions,' he uses them to sustain the clan's independent status. Although the clan currently remains independent and swears fealty to no kingdom, Yildirim's underworld reputation and consummate guerrilla tactics have made the Karakhergit a feared power on the steppe, forever guarding the last nomadic freedom of this land.
